title: The Burnt Deadline Revisited
premise: Beatrix Reyes, a veteran interpreter for a fragile peace delegation, has survived a decade of dangerous negotiations by keeping one secret: she once translated a massacre order into diplomatic language instead of the truth, saving her own life and damning a village. When a burner phone that should not exist begins ringing with the voice of Tomas, the delegation's dead security chief, she realizes someone is weaponizing her guilt — and the summit convenes in nine days. As the caller forces her to trade the secret worth killing for, Beatrix discovers Tomas faked his death to expose the delegation's own broker of the massacre, and that her polished lie is the only evidence that can convict him. In the end, Beatrix testifies at the summit, burning her career, her alias, and her safety to tell the truth she buried, walking out alive but unrecognizable to herself.
about_author: Dominic Brightwater is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in ceasefire corridors before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose professions demand fluent lies.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Beatrix Reyes, POV. Arriving in Geneva for a doomed summit, she checks into a safehouse hotel, rehearses her cover story in the mirror, and confirms her go-bag is packed. The emotional beat is controlled dread — a woman whose entire life is a rehearsed escape.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. The delegation's first planning session reveals fractures: the minister wants concessions, the broker Aurelio Voss wants leverage. Beatrix translates a threat dressed as courtesy and feels the old machinery of her lie begin to turn.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. A burner phone appears in her coat pocket — a phone she never bought. It rings. The voice is Tomas, her security chief, dead eleven months. He says only: 'You kept the receipt.' The beat is vertigo; her polished reality cracks.

chapters.title: Dead Men Dial Collect
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV, investigating. She verifies the call's origin: a relay routed through the delegation's own comms suite. Tomas knew things only an insider knew. Paranoia blooms — is the delegation hunting her, or protecting her?

chapters.title: What the Interpreter Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Beatrix's memory. Ten years ago in Kavaje, she translated a colonel's order to 'clear' a village as a 'security relocation' for the record. The lie saved her life. The chapter ends with her waking, present-day, shaking.

chapters.title: Voss's Smile
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Broker Aurelio Voss invites her to dinner and probes, too precisely, about Kavaje. She realizes someone has been feeding him fragments. The emotional beat is the hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: The Second Call
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Tomas calls again: bring the original transcript from the Kavaje file, or he releases recordings implicating her. She refuses — then finds her safehouse searched, the go-bag rifled but nothing taken except a photograph of the village.

chapters.title: Lena in the Lobby
chapters.summary: Lena Okafor, delegation archivist, POV. Lena has noticed files moving in the archive under Tomas's old credentials — credentials that were supposedly revoked at his death. Her beat: quiet competence curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Archive at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She breaks into the delegation archive and finds Tomas's death report altered — the dental records don't match. He may be alive. Hope arrives like a knife: if he's alive, he chose to let her believe he was dead.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Voss offers her a deal: confirm the Kavaje transcript's authenticity and he'll bury her name in it. She understands he needs her lie to legitimize his cover-up. Loyalty, truth, survival — she can only keep two.

chapters.title: The Man in the Rain
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. A dead-drop meeting: a hooded figure she believes is Tomas. It's a trap — Voss's men. She escapes through the old town using tradecraft Tomas taught her, realizing the real Tomas would never have set a trap this clumsy.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Listening
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena decrypts the comms relay and discovers a third party has been spoofing Tomas's voice with AI synthesis — someone who has her old recordings. She hesitates over whether to warn Beatrix, whom she half-suspects.

chapters.title: The Voice Lesson
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She replays the calls and hears what she missed: the pauses are wrong, the breathing is synthetic. Tomas may be dead after all — but someone with access to his voice wants her secret badly enough to resurrect him.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Lena, alternating POV. They form a wary alliance. Lena reveals the spoofed calls originate from inside the minister's inner circle. The beat: two women who trust no one choosing, provisionally, to trust each other.

chapters.title: The Minister's Quiet Man
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She traces the relay to Deputy Chief Ilsa Brandt, the minister's fixer — the same officer who delivered the Kavaje order a decade ago. Brandt isn't covering the massacre up. She's protecting the man who gave it.

chapters.title: What Tomas Actually Did
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena finds Tomas's real last assignment: he had discovered the Kavaje order and was bringing it to Beatrix when he died — not faked, not murdered by Voss, but killed in an 'accident' arranged by Brandt. The beat is grief with a purpose.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Voss, cornered by her knowledge, threatens the delegation itself: testify and the summit collapses, the ceasefire dies, people she knows die with it. The lie, she realizes, has been holding up the peace — a rotten keystone.

chapters.title: The Original Transcript
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. She retrieves the Kavaje original from the hiding place only she and Tomas knew — sewn into the lining of the go-bag she has carried, packed, for ten years. The beat: the escape kit was always the evidence.

chapters.title: Night Before the Summit
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Lena, alternating. Brandt corners Beatrix with a gun and an offer of quiet exile. Beatrix stalls, records the threat, and barely survives when Lena triggers the building's alarm. The beat: terror transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Floor of the Summit
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. As the plenary opens, she abandons her interpreter's booth, walks to the floor, and requests the floor as a witness. Voss moves to have her removed; she begins reading the Kavaje order aloud — this time, translating it truthfully.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The transcript detonates the summit: Voss arrested, the minister complicit, Brandt's recording played into the record. The ceasefire collapses — but the lie that propped it up is dead. Beatrix's beat: ruin and relief in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Bag
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV, epilogue. Months later, living under no alias at all, she unpacks the go-bag for the first time in a decade and donates the contents. She is unemployed, exposed, and finally fluent in her own voice. The beat: the price of survival, paid and survived.
